readability.reviewer: Coding agent (Claude Code), the primary session; no independent human or model review
readability.summary: The four new TypeScript modules open with what they are for, which part of the Desktop UI contract they serve and where their boundary to the foundation runs: each says what Theia provides and what the file adds. Comments say why a choice exists where the code alone would not: why the toggles run Theia's commands and take their state from the sidebars, why the right sidebar's tabs are connected as Theia connects a side bar's with two named exceptions, why the first layout waits for the left sidebar before it shows the right one, why the title row's items are laid out as one line, and why a stored area the version does not know is refused. The design-token script states its new rule for shares, and the tests name the behaviour they prove. Review against the final code renamed a method that hid one of the foundation's, replaced destructured token names by the full names the token test looks for, removed a style rule the foundation already has and one that had no effect, stopped exporting a list nothing imports, let the logo file be named once for the About dialog and the title row, and rewrote one comment in plain characters. The end-to-end test was made to fail a check instead of timing out where a seeded defect showed it would, and to wait for the loading screen to go before it clicks (TASK-011_EVIDENCE.md sections 9 and 11).

cleanup.summary: TASK-011 created no temporary artifact inside the checkout: every command that imports a checkout module ran with -B, Cargo built into /mnt/F/Nexees-toolchains/target/, the Desktop window was built in its desktop/ folder there and installed for testing in desktop-install/ and, for one observation, a second time in desktop-install-earlier/, which the observing script removed again, the private profiles of the end-to-end test and of the debugging sessions lived in the system temporary folder and were removed by the sessions themselves, and the negative-test copies, the seeded-defect copy of the test, the measuring and observing scripts and the evidence scripts used the session scratch folder. Temporary lines that measured the first layout were put into one source file and one test file during the work and taken out again before any log of this folder was written; the corroboration searches the files a commit would hold and finds no trace of them. At the close, scripts/test/task_cleanup.py ran on the checkout with an empty TASK-011 manifest, first as a plan and then with --apply and its record: it removed nothing, refused nothing, and left in place 24 untracked files, the four new source files and the TASK-011 evidence, each with its hash. The ignored files are the owner's IDE output (rust-analyzer's target/ and the Java extension's .gradle/ beside TASK-003's prototype) and the editor's link apps/desktop/node_modules, none task-owned, all left exactly as they are. The disposable installation and the scratch files of this task are removed once this receipt is committed and pushed; the Desktop build folder stays beside the Cargo target folder as a build cache, and the copy of the evidence scripts in /mnt/F/Nexees-toolchains/task-tools/ stays for the rest of this run of tasks. No pre-existing or user-owned file was deleted, reset or stashed; the owner's logo file was only read. One file of the owner's was changed by mistake: one command of the task ran its lockfile check without the isolated toolchain, so the system's cargo ran it with the owner's cargo home, offline and in a scratch copy, and updated its bookkeeping file ~/.cargo/.global-cache. No other file of the owner's toolchain and cache folders was written by a command of the task (TASK-011_EVIDENCE.md sections 10 and 11).

owner_decision.question: TASK-011 is built and every check passes, but one of my commands ran the system's cargo against your ~/.cargo by mistake, and cargo rewrote its bookkeeping file ~/.cargo/.global-cache (when cached files were last used). Nothing else there was written and nothing was downloaded, but the earlier content is gone. The truthful receipt says so and the acceptance program refuses it (validate.scope). How should I resolve this?
owner_decision.answer_text: You accept the rewritten ~/.cargo/.global-cache as the current state of your cargo home. I record your decision in TASK-011's receipt as the reason, set no_unrelated_changes back to true, clear the blocker and re-run the acceptance. The deviation stays disclosed. Then I commit and push TASK-011, clean up and go on with TASK-012.
owner_decision.basis: The owner accepts the rewritten ~/.cargo/.global-cache (196,608 bytes, last written 2026-10-05 11:59:46, SHA-256 629c9c181a22298660214ca7619faae3b9efcc5d19972757884a61db1709133a, unchanged when the decision was recorded) as the current state of the owner's cargo home. The change was a side effect of one command of TASK-011 that ran without the isolated toolchain. It is disclosed in TASK-011_EVIDENCE.md sections 10 and 11, in logs/ide_activity.txt and in receipt/final_verification.txt, and with this approval no unapproved change to the owner's pre-existing work remains.
